questions.question: How does JavaScript property lookup use the prototype chain?
keyPoints: Check the value's own properties first
Follow its prototype if a key is missing
Continue until a property is found or the chain ends
Reading inherited data does not copy it onto the value
questions.modelAnswer: JavaScript first checks an object's own properties. If the requested key is absent, lookup follows its prototype and continues until it finds the property or reaches the end of the chain.

questions.question: What do extends and super provide in class inheritance?
keyPoints: A derived constructor must call super before using this
questions.modelAnswer: extends declares a subclass relationship, allowing instances to inherit behavior through the prototype chain. super lets subclass code call parent constructors or methods, and a derived constructor must call super before using this.

questions.question: What does instanceof check, and what should callers keep in mind?
keyPoints: It checks the constructor prototype in the chain
It is not a structural shape check
Different realms can have different built-in constructors
Custom prototype changes can affect the result
questions.modelAnswer: instanceof checks whether a constructor's prototype occurs in a value's prototype chain; it does not verify the value's shape. Values created in another realm or with a modified prototype chain can behave differently from simple expectations.
